title: Reading Drill — Surveying arrivals at a public pool — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Surveying arrivals at a public pool — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Bramley, work on families reaching the ticket counter just before classes change had already produced a small collection of entrance counts. The pool supervisor used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the length of the peak queue.

**B** The group kept staggered start times for the new trial, which was planned to run for eight weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that changes in class size should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
